# Editability standards — review gate number one, WordPress version

> **Cross-phase packet, applies from Phase 3 to Phase 9.** Read once at the start of a run, read again in Phase 8b. The T4 version was drawn
> from the runs where JoomlArt reviewers **rejected** a build; this version keeps the same reason — the buyer is the one who edits
> in the admin, never in code — and switches the mechanism to WordPress.

## One rule that pulls every other rule

> **For every piece of text / image / link / section, ask: "can the site owner change this in the admin, without code?"**
> No → it is built wrong. Turn it into `post_content` (a block with `role: content`), a synced pattern,
> `wp_navigation`, or site identity.

How to check: open the page in the block editor or the Site Editor and click the thing. If it cannot be clicked, or clicking opens
a code modal, it fails.

## 1. WHERE text may live

| Kind of text | Right place | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Page content, marketing sections (hero, features, pricing, FAQ, CTA…) | the page's `post_content` | the pattern is inserted as a copy; each text/image/link cell is a block with `metadata.role = content` ([`templates-and-patterns.md`](templates-and-patterns.md) §3) |
| Posts | the post's `post_content` | block markup (generated by `html-to-blocks.mjs`) |
| A block repeated in many places, edit once to change everywhere (contact info, demo notice, footer text) | **synced pattern** (`wp_block`) | `<!-- wp:block {"ref":N} /-->` |
| Menus, navigation links, footer link columns | a **`wp_navigation`** post | `core/navigation {"ref":N}` |
| Site name, tagline, logo | site identity | `core/site-title` ← `blogname`, `core/site-tagline` ← `blogdescription`, `core/site-logo` ← theme mod `custom_logo` |
| 404 page text (and the shared empty-state message) | a **synced pattern** (`wp_block`) referenced by `templates/404.html` | WordPress has no post for the 404 view: the copy lives in a `wp_block` (`<!-- wp:block {"ref":N} /-->`), text in the database. Copy written into `templates/404.html` is baked like any other template text (gotcha 44) |
| A few stray fields tied to one page (address, opening hours) | post meta + Block Bindings `core/post-meta` | needs `register_meta(show_in_rest)` — a plugin's job; not used in Tracy Base yet |

## 2. What is NOT acceptable

- **Text baked into a template or part.** `templates/*.html` holds only structural blocks (post-title,
  post-content, query, search); `parts/*.html` holds only chrome. Parts are editable in the Site Editor, but the
  customer's edit is saved in the DB and **overrides** the theme file — so text in a part is both hard to find and loses later fixes.
  Chrome text that needs translating/editing goes through a PHP pattern or a synced pattern.
- **`core/html` for text.** The site owner can only edit it in a code modal; `<script>`/`<iframe>` are filtered by `wp_kses`
  for users without `unfiltered_html` ([`inputs/from-joomla.md`](inputs/from-joomla.md) §10). Use it only
  for truly raw HTML that cannot be expressed in blocks, and list each spot in `content-gaps.md`.
  `html-to-blocks.mjs` falls back to `core/html` when it meets `style=` or `table`/`iframe`/`form` — each fallback is
  an item to decide, not a default.
- **Hand-typed menu `<a>`** (in a list, paragraph, button) instead of `core/navigation` pointing to `wp_navigation`:
  no "current", no menu management, a slug change breaks it. A header CTA button may be a `core/button`
  (editable in the part) but its target must follow the real page.
- **Text outside `role: content`** in a pattern: WordPress 7.0 inserts patterns as `contentOnly`, and a block
  without a role is a block the customer cannot touch.
- **Hand-drawn SVG/CSS images** for a complex picture (dashboard, chart): it must be a `core/image` with a file
  in the media library so the site owner can replace it. Simple icons/logos stay SVG.
- **Dead forms.** A contact/newsletter form is a plugin (Q10: Contact Form 7, GPL) or absent; a `<form>`
  that submits nowhere is a defect, record a gap.
- **CPTs in the theme.** `register_post_type` in a theme is plugin territory and is lost on a theme switch; structured lists
  (team, testimonials) are a pattern with N `role: content` cards, or posts in one category +
  Query Loop (`section-team-query`).

## 3. Clean menus

- Each Joomla site menu → one `wp_navigation`; administrator menus (`client_id 1`) are not exported.
- Internal links are `kind: post-type` + the page's `id` (so the current page can be marked); gaps point to
  `redirectTo`; only external URLs are `kind: custom`.
- Admin tree == visible nav: no hidden items, no duplicates pointing to the same page, no leftover scaffold.
- Account links: the page seeded for the account view when the page-map has one; an account view
  with no seeded page falls back to `wp-login.php` and its `?action=` variants (Q9); a URL with no
  view in the page-map keeps its source URL — no placeholder pages.

## 4. Names findable in the admin

- Pages and posts: `post_title` is the source title; the slug is generated from the title (D2) — do not carry over sample-data aliases.
- Synced patterns (`wp_block`): `post_title` = `[<Theme>] <Page> - <Part>` (`[Tracy Base] Footer - Contact
  information`) so they can be filtered in Patterns.
- `wp_navigation`: `post_title` = the source menu name (`Tracy`, `Tracy utility`).
- Blocks in a pattern: `metadata.name` per the `patterns.map.json` convention.

## 5. Render / function gate (measured live, light + dark, desktop + mobile)

Search returns real results; pagination renders (no tofu); button hover is right (no global `a:hover`); no
horizontal overflow; the mega menu is reachable with the mouse (`scripts/review/mega-hover.mjs --items '.tracy-mega'`).

## 6. Demo content gate

One topic, one voice; real posts, no stubs, no lorem; on-topic images; `demo.disclosure` shows
on every surface in `demo` mode ([`content-contract.md`](content-contract.md)). Missing → leave it empty and record it in
`content-gaps.md` — inventing is worse than leaving empty.

## 7. How to audit (Phase 8b, agent `editability`)

For each page in the page-map: (1) `wp post get <id> --field=post_content` — count `core/html` blocks, count
blocks with text but without `role: content`; (2) `wp post list --post_type=wp_navigation` — each
`core/navigation` in a part has a `ref` pointing to an existing post; (3) grep `parts/*.html` and `templates/*.html`
of the **installed tree** for text outside structural blocks; (4) open the Site Editor and try clicking one piece of text per section. The verdict
is a named list of violations (page, block, rule §), or "clean". There is no "looks fine".

`review/editability.mjs` reads where each run is drawn. A run whose every occurrence sits inside
`.wp-block-post-content` is that post's own text: it is not matched against `templates/`, so a page
body is not blamed on a template that happens to say the same words. It is still matched against
`parts/` and `patterns/`, and one occurrence outside the post content is enough to match the
templates. The verdict counts these runs as `inContent`. A `--theme` directory that does not exist
exits 2; an empty theme would pass every run.
